text:
ravi: heads up — we're seeing intermittent packet loss between pods on gpu nodes in us-west2. jobs hitting gRPC RSTs and retries. started ~04:12 UTC, spikes every ~4-8m for 20-40s.
cheng: ugh. only on gpu nodes? or all nodes in that AZ?
ravi: seems limited to nodes labeled gpu=true, east-west traffic (same node pairs). control plane fine. pod->svc cross-node flakes.
emily: any recent kernel or NIC driver rollouts in that fleet?
ravi: kernel bumped to 6.1.4 on the gpu pool last night; non-gpu pool still on 5.15. also we rolled a kube-proxy image for conntrack tuning last week.
sam: can you share a short pcap or mtr? also what's MTU on the overlay?
ravi: collecting tcpdump now. overlay is geneve, node MTU 9000, geneve tunnel MTU 8950.
sre-oncall: tagging infra oncall: @cheng @sam :eyes:
cheng: run `sudo ip netns exec cali-xyz tcpdump -nne -s 0 -c 200 host <peer-pod-ip> and not icmp` on source and on dest at same time. also `ss -s` for retransmits.
emily: quick check: `ethtool -k ens*` — confirm GRO/GSO/LRO states. last time we saw similar spikes it was GRO coalescing on encap boundary causing reorder.
ravi: tcpdump attached (small excerpt):
```
18:04:12.123456 IP 10.3.15.9.44393 > 10.3.9.21.9090: Flags [P.], seq 1:145, ack 1, win 501, length 144
18:04:12.123478 IP 10.3.15.9.44393 > 10.3.9.21.9090: Flags [.], seq 145:289, ack 1, win 501, length 144
18:04:12.143000 IP 10.3.9.21.9090 > 10.3.15.9.44393: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```
cheng: RSTs on server side — app might be dropping due to partial packet delivery. check kernel dmesg for NIC driver warnings.
sam: also check encapsulation interface counters: `ip -s link show geneve0` and inner device `ip -s link show tunl0` (name depends). looking for rx errors/discards.
ravi: output: `ip -s link show geneve0` shows RX: 0 errors but RX packets with dropped 120 in 1m window.
emily: try disabling GRO/GSO on the physical NIC temporarily as a hypothesis: `sudo ethtool -K ens7 gro off gso off tx offload off` and see if spike stops. painful but quick to test on one node.
sam: we should also run `iperf3 -c` between pods (udp + tcp) during a spike, and `tracepath` to see PMTU.
sre-oncall: rolling a single node out for test in staging-gpu pool to avoid impacting prod.
ravi: running ethtool changes now on node gpu-node-12.
ops-bot: deploybot: started cordon/drain of gpu-node-12 for test at 04:28 UTC.
cheng: if disabling offloads stabilizes it, we likely have an encap-offload interaction with NIC driver + geneve checksum handling. last time fix was a kernel NIC patch.
emily: worth checking if RDMA is enabled on these nodes; RDMA + encapsulation has known corner cases with offloads. `rdma hw` status?
sam: also double-check multiqueue hash changes — ECMP flow rebalancing can create transient reordering that looks like loss for TCP. any BGP/underlay changes around 04:10–04:20?
ravi: nothing in change logs. but we did autoscale backfills around 04:06 which created a burst of pod churn.
cheng: autoscale burst + conntrack + encap offloads = good recipe for partial drops. could be conntrack table thrash as well. `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` during spike?
ravi: conntrack_count jumped from 18k to 92k during burst. thresholds at 100k.
emily: that's high. conntrack timeouts on short-lived flows could be evicting entries and causing unexpected RSTs. consider raising `nf_conntrack_max` or adjust `tcp_syn_retries` if needed.
sam: ok prioritized checklist: 1) disable GRO/GSO on one test node, 2) capture simultaneous tcpdump from both ends during a spike, 3) run iperf3 udp to measure packet loss, 4) monitor conntrack count and dmesg, 5) if repro, try pinning overlay to vxlan as A/B test.
ravi: did step 1 — turned off offloads on gpu-node-12. initial look: no spikes for last 6 min.
cheng: promising. schedule a controlled test: disable offloads on 3 nodes and run backfill workload to reproduce. if stable, prepare kernel/driver rollback or upstream patch.
emily: also file a bug with NIC vendor with pcap and `ethtool -k` outputs. include kernel version and geneve config.
sam: note cost/ops impact: disabling offloads increases CPU on host for packet processing. we might need to offset with a higher instance size temporarily for Dedicated clusters.
sre-oncall: creating incident ticket with links to pcaps and notes.
ops-bot: incidentbot: INC-2026-134 opened for intermittent geneve loss (assigned to eng-runtime).
ravi: thanks team. will run the controlled three-node test 05:10 UTC and report results here.
cheng: if test is green, plan next steps: node image pin to old kernel for gpu fleet, or coordinate vendor kernel patch and roll forward.
emily: also add a short-run eval in Redwood Optimize to detect similar regression patterns in future: correlate conntrack + offload flag changes with packet loss events.
sam: +1.
cheng: update: attached grep of `dmesg` from gpu-node-12 shows `mlx5_core: WARNING: droppping fragments` — filing with vendor.
ravi: test completed — three-node batch ran for 30m without observed gRPC RSTs. rolling to canary pool now.
emily: great. keep PCAPs and offload toggles in incident ticket for postmortem. :thumbsup:
sam: minor follow-up — we should add a health alert in console for per-node geneve rx-drops > 50/min.
sre-oncall: noted. closing loop once canary completes.
ops-bot: deploybot: uncordon gpu-node-12 at 05:55 UTC.
ravi: closing for now, will post postmortem after vendor ticket and canary roll.
